page: Amazon Web Services m5n.4xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The instance achieved average ratings in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU tests, and Geekbench multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, also fall within the average range. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-quartile results in single-core stress-ng, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression tests. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5n.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads requiring moderate compute and memory resources without the premium of specialized hardware. The average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving makes it a viable option for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications such as software compilation, image processing, web serving, and moderate database operations, though it may be less optimal for single-thread-intensive tasks or workloads requiring local NVMe storage.
